doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Drugs and the House of Correction
title: The Calumet City strip joints and Jive Jackson
summary: Ware plays drums for strip acts in Calumet City in a band whose leader supplied pills to keep his habit going.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: The strip joints . See, everybody at one time worked out there. Vernell was working down the street, Ike had in fact, he showed me how to play one lady's act -- a lady called Tanalia -- she worked with snakes -- a mystic type thing, alligator -- we had 5 pieces out there. And the guy that had the bag was called Jive Jackson, a trumpet player -- bless his soul. Jive had the bag. He didn't have nothing but junkies in his band, all except the tenor player -- he didn't fool around.

But the piano player, myself, Jive -- well, he was the leader; he had the bag. Now, he was selling pills and would give us each 2 pills before we go to work and 2 pills when we got off work, and made sure he paid our rent -- we didn't have no pocket change to buy some cigarettes or anything -- and we were happy.
We worked from 9 until daylight. And Jive was making all the money. We didn't question it, so long as he kept our habits up, you know. And had a roof over our head.
